newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates close lower as fund eases.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates close lower as fund eases.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates closed lower on Friday as a result of persistant efforts by the central bank to inject funds into the banking system to ease liquidity, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate closed to 7.772 percent against Thursday's 8.240 finish -- but still well above the central bank's previously declared 5.0-5.5 target zone.
The 30-day commercial paper slid to 7.35-50 against 7.50.
Responding to banking system's liquidity squeeze, the central bank has repeatedly injected funds into the banking system through open market operations in recent days.
Friday was no exceptation. The bank injected T$300 million funds into the banking system.
A central bank official said the bank also released T$5 billion in interests of state postal funds to fuel the starved banking system with more liquidity.
With these moves, dealers expected the money rates to continue to fall.
In the bond market, the benchmark 10-year 86/4 bond yield stabilised at 6.1075 percent.
